text_en: Once while Jesus was standing beside the lake of Gennesaret, and the crowd was pressing in on him to hear the word of God,
text_cn: 有一次，耶稣站在革乃撒勒湖边，群众拥到他前要听天主的道理。

text_en: he saw two boats there at the shore of the lake; the fishermen had gone out of them and were washing their nets.
text_cn: 他看见两只船在湖边停着，渔夫下了船正在洗网。

text_en: He got into one of the boats, the one belonging to Simon, and asked him to put out a little way from the shore. Then he sat down and taught the crowds from the boat.
text_cn: 他上了其中一只属于西满的船，请他把船稍微划开，离开陆地；耶稣就坐下，从船上教训群众。

text_en: When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, “Put out into the deep water and let down your nets for a catch. ”
text_cn: 一讲完了，就对西满说：“划到深处去，撒你们的网捕鱼罢！”

text_en: Simon answered, “Master, we have worked all night long but have caught nothing. Yet if you say so, I will let down the nets. ”
text_cn: 西满回答说：“老师，我们已整夜劳苦，毫无所获；但我要遵照你的话撒网。”

text_en: When they had done this, they caught so many fish that their nets were beginning to break.
text_cn: 他们照样办了，网了许多鱼，网险些破裂了。

text_en: So they signaled their partners in the other boat to come and help them. And they came and filled both boats, so that they began to sink.
text_cn: 他们遂招呼别只船上的同伴来协助他们。他们来到，装满了两只船，以致船也几乎下沉。

text_en: But when Simon Peter saw it, he fell down at Jesus’ knees, saying, “Go away from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man! ”
text_cn: 西满伯多禄一见这事，就跪伏在耶稣膝前说：“主，请你离开我！因为我是个罪人。”

text_en: For he and all who were with him were amazed at the catch of fish that they had taken;
text_cn: 西满和同他一起的人，因了他们所捕的鱼，都惊骇起来；

text_en: and so also were James and John, sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon. Then Jesus said to Simon, “Do not be afraid; from now on you will be catching people. ”
text_cn: 他的伙伴，即载伯德的儿子雅各伯和若望，也一样惊骇。耶稣对西满说：“不要害怕！从今以后，你要做捕人的渔夫！”

text_en: When they had brought their boats to shore, they left everything and followed him.
text_cn: 他们把船划到岸边，就舍弃一切，跟随了他。

text_en: Once, when he was in one of the cities, there was a man covered with leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he bowed with his face to the ground and begged him, “Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean. ”
text_cn: 有一次，耶稣在一座城里，看，有一个遍体长癞的人，见了耶稣，就俯首至地求他说：“主，你若愿意，就能洁净我。”

text_en: Then Jesus stretched out his hand, touched him, and said, “I do choose. Be made clean. ” Immediately the leprosy left him.
text_cn: 耶稣便伸手抚摸他说：“我愿意，你洁净了罢！”癞病就立刻由他身上退去。

text_en: And he ordered him to tell no one. “Go, ” he said, “and show yourself to the priest, and, as Moses commanded, make an offering for your cleansing, for a testimony to them. ”
text_cn: 耶稣切切嘱咐他不要告诉别人，并说：“但要去叫司祭检验你，为你的洁净，献上梅瑟所规定的，给他们当作证据。”

text_en: But now more than ever the word about Jesus spread abroad; many crowds would gather to hear him and to be cured of their diseases.
text_cn: 他的名声更传扬开了，遂有许多人齐集来听教，并为治好自己的病症。

text_en: But he would withdraw to deserted places and pray.
text_cn: 耶稣却退入荒野中去祈祷。

text_en: One day, while he was teaching, Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting near by (they had come from every village of Galilee and Judea and from Jerusalem); and the power of the Lord was with him to heal.
text_cn: 有一天，耶稣正在施教，几个法利塞人和法学士也在座，他们是从加里肋亚和犹太各乡村及耶路撒冷来的；上主的德能催迫他治病。

text_en: Just then some men came, carrying a paralyzed man on a bed. They were trying to bring him in and lay him before Jesus;
text_cn: 看，有人用床抬来一个患瘫痪症的人，设法把他抬进去，放在耶稣跟前；

text_en: but finding no way to bring him in because of the crowd, they went up on the roof and let him down with his bed through the tiles into the middle of the crowd in front of Jesus.
text_cn: 但因人众多，不得其门而入，遂上了房顶，从瓦中间，把他连那小床系到中间，正放在耶稣面前。

text_en: When he saw their faith, he said, “Friend, your sins are forgiven you. ”
text_cn: 耶稣一见他们的信心，就说：“人啊！你的罪赦了。”

text_en: Then the scribes and the Pharisees began to question, “Who is this who is speaking blasphemies? Who can forgive sins but God alone? ”
text_cn: 经师和法利塞人开始忖度（cǔn duó）说：“这人是谁？竟说亵渎话！除了天主一个外，谁能赦罪？”

text_en: When Jesus perceived their questionings, he answered them, “Why do you raise such questions in your hearts?
text_cn: 耶稣看透了他们的心思，就向他们说：“你们心里忖度什么呢？

text_en: Which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven you, ’ or to say, ‘Stand up and walk’?
text_cn: 什么比较容易？是说：你的罪赦了，或是说：起来行走罢！

text_en: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the one who was paralyzed—“I say to you, stand up and take your bed and go to your home. ”
text_cn: 但为叫你们知道人子在地上有权赦罪──便对瘫子说：我给你说：起来，拿起你的小床，回家去罢！”

text_en: Immediately he stood up before them, took what he had been lying on, and went to his home, glorifying God.
text_cn: 那人立刻在他们面前站了起来，拿着他躺过的小床，赞颂着天主，回家去了。

text_en: Amazement seized all of them, and they glorified God and were filled with awe, saying, “We have seen strange things today. ”
text_cn: 众人十分惊奇，并光荣天主，满怀恐惧说：“今天我们看见了出奇的事。”

text_en: After this he went out and saw a tax collector named Levi, sitting at the tax booth; and he said to him, “Follow me. ”
text_cn: 此后，耶稣出去，看见一个税吏，名叫肋未，在税关那里坐着，便对他说：“跟随我罢！”

text_en: And he got up, left everything, and followed him.
text_cn: 他便舍弃一切，起来跟随了他。

text_en: Then Levi gave a great banquet for him in his house; and there was a large crowd of tax collectors and others sitting at the table with them.
text_cn: 肋未在自己家中为他摆设了盛筵，有许多税吏和其他的人，与他们一同坐席。

text_en: The Pharisees and their scribes were complaining to his disciples, saying, “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners? ”
text_cn: 法利塞人和他们的经师就愤愤不平，对他的门徒说：“你们为什么同税吏和罪人一起吃喝？”

text_en: Jesus answered, “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick;
text_cn: 耶稣回答他们说：“不是健康的人需要医生，而是有病的人。

text_en: I have come to call not the righteous but sinners to repentance. ”
text_cn: 我不是来召叫义人，而是召叫罪人悔改。”

text_en: Then they said to him, “John’s disciples, like the disciples of the Pharisees, frequently fast and pray, but your disciples eat and drink. ”
text_cn: 他们又对他说：“若翰的门徒屡次禁食，行祈祷；法利塞人的门徒也是这样；而你的门徒却又吃又喝。”

text_en: Jesus said to them, “You cannot make wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them, can you?
text_cn: 耶稣回答说：“伴郎与新郎在一起的时候，你们岂能叫他们禁食？

text_en: The days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast in those days. ”
text_cn: 但日子将要来到，当新郎从他们中被劫去时，在那些日子，他们就要禁食了。”

text_en: He also told them a parable: “No one tears a piece from a new garment and sews it on an old garment; otherwise the new will be torn, and the piece from the new will not match the old.
text_cn: 他又对他们讲比喻说：“没有人从新衣服上撕下一块作补钉，补在旧衣上的；不然，新的撕破了，而且从新衣上撕下的补钉，与旧的也不相称。

text_en: And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the new wine will burst the skins and will be spilled, and the skins will be destroyed.
text_cn: 也没有人把新酒装入旧皮囊的；不然，新酒要涨破皮囊，酒要流出来，皮囊也破了。

text_en: But new wine must be put into fresh wineskins.
text_cn: 但新酒应装入新囊。

text_en: And no one after drinking old wine desires new wine, but says, ‘The old is good. ’”
text_cn: 也没有人喝着陈酒，愿意喝新酒的，因为他说：还是陈的好。”
